Tom Griffin November 25, 2019 Tom Griffin was appointed Director for the Office of Financial and Audit Management in August 2019. In this role, he manages CFO’s Financial and Audit Management functions with the overall objective of improving DOE business operations. Mr. Griffin has served in various management and policy roles for the Department of Energy. He joined DOE in 2009 as a Team Leader for the Office of Inspector General and was appointed an Assistant Director for Risk Management within the Office of the CFO during DOE’s implementation of the Recovery Act. He has also served as the Division Director for Financial Policy within the Office of the CFO and a Risk Management Analyst for the Office of Acquisition Management with responsibilities for internal controls, audit resolution, and financial assistance policy. Prior to joining DOE, Mr. Griffin worked for the Office of Inspector General at the Department of Commerce, where he led inspections of overseas Foreign Commercial Service posts and program evaluations of domestic Commerce programs. Christchurch, Canterbury, South Island, New Zealand © Travelscape Images / Alamy Stock Photo SCIENCE LAELAPS Top Jurassic Carnivore Had an Amazing Gape By Riley Black Published November 23, 2015 • 9 min read Tyrannosaurus rex is the ultimate in Mesozoic clickbait. You could even say that it’s a real tyrant , casting a large shadow over the hundreds of other dinosaurs that could benefit from some time in the spotlight. So even though paleontologist Stephan Lautenschlager included T. rex in his new study on dinosaur bites, I don’t want to talk about the tyrant lizard king much. I want to focus on a different lizard. Long time readers know that I have a soft spot for Allosaurus . The 150 million year old dinosaur was the top carnivore of the Late Jurassic, reaching sizes to rival that of the later T. rex and was much more common than its toothy neighbors Ceratosaurus and Torvosaurus . And as estimated by Lautenschlager, Allosaurus also had one of the most impressive bites of all time. Working from virtual models of Tyrannosaurus , Allosaurus , and the herbivorous theropod Erlikosaurus fitted with digital jaw muscles based on the anatomy of buzzards and alligators, Lautenschlager estimated the optimal and maximum gapes for the three dinosaurs. She had arrived. And with her, she carried genuine joy and light. Backed by an all-woman band of Tiny Desk alumnae, Kelly effortlessly moves through songs from her latest album, God Must Really Love Me . The record captures Kelly in the present: reflecting on her faith journey and navigating life as a new mom. She also drops some gems for the day one's, including brief tastes of "Nobody Love" and "Dear No One." But, most serendipitously for the middle schoolers in attendance, Kelly performs her rendition of Stevie Wonder 's "Don't You Worry 'Bout a Thing," the song that her character Meena belts in the animated film Sing . Beyond her anointing as a vocalist and musician, she has endured the many shifts of the music industry while maintaining an authenticity that cuts through the noise and reaches the heart. There's something special about watching an artist who has grown so much, yet still sounds and feels unmistakably like herself. pages.text: Tracking a Mystery: When and How the First Americans Arrived | National Geographic The Oregon Coast, pictured here, may have been a byway for the first Americans as they followed the nutrient-rich coast southward on foot and by boat, says the new book, Atlas of a Lost World . Photograph by Ty Milford, Aurora BOOK TALK When, How Did the First Americans Arrive? It’s Complicated. The first Americans weren't one group of people; they arrived at different times, and likely by different methods. By Simon Worrall Published June 9, 2018 • 13 min read How did human beings first come to North America? Across the Bering Strait, on foot? Down the “kelp highway” by boat? Across the Atlantic via the polar ice cap? And when did they reach here? 10,000 years ago? 40,000? Or were they always here, as the Navajo and other Native American tribes believe? In his new book, Atlas Of A Lost World , author Craig Childs sets off to test these different theories on the ground, traveling from Alaska to Chile, Canada to Florida. What he finds, despite the best efforts of archaeologists and the latest technology , still remains in many ways a mystery. Speaking from his home in Colorado, he explains why many Native Americans reject the idea that their ancestors migrated from somewhere else; how an archaeologist nicknamed Dr. Poop believes he has identified the first human excrement in America ; and why diversity seems to have been built into America’s DNA. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/feature-stories/trial-fire-look-nist-fire-testing-through-years Credit: © Earl Zubkoff Trial by Fire: A Look at NIST Fire Testing Through the Years March 6, 2018 Facebook Linkedin X.com Email Fire testing may have started some 2.5 million years ago when one of our ancestors stuck his hand into the first flame and “scientifically” determined that the temperature was too hot to bear. Since that primitive beginning, humans have been on an unending quest to understand, measure and exploit the behavior of fire — and most importantly, to improve our ability to protect life and property from its ravages. Fire testing at NIST, a staple of the agency’s research since the early 1900s, has helped provide much of the data, insights and knowledge demanded by that pursuit. Find out more about NIST's fire research and the National Fire Research Laboratory . Credit: NIST Digital Archives NIST conducted what may have been America’s first full-scale fire test when researchers burned down two condemned buildings in Washington, D.C., on June 17, 1928. Data from this experiment, along with previous work by pioneer fire researcher Simon H. Ingberg, eventually led to uniform fire resistance standards for buildings.

Trouble Funk: Tiny Desk Concert May 30, 2018 12:00 PM ET By Abby O'Neill Credit: NPR Go-go — Washington D.C.'s regional twist on funk — reigned in the DMV during the 1980s, and one of the scene's signature acts was Trouble Funk. More than 30 years later, the collective, led by Big Tony Fisher, still fills sold-out venues with heavyweight percussion and call-and-response lyrics. Trouble Funk concerts are bona fide jam sessions, so I was determined to squeeze their unrelenting rhythms behind the Tiny Desk. With 12 members sandwiched into a cramped space, the electricity was almost tangible as they launched into the 1982 banger "Pump Me Up," a song sampled in Public Enemy's protest anthem "Fight the Power" and M/A/R/R/S's dance classic "Pump Up The Volume." The drum breaks here are definitive go-go and it was hard to discern who was having more fun: the band or the audience. On "Grip It," buoyant and staccato horn melodies propelled the song forward, while "Let's Get Small" featured Trouble Funk's classic call-and-response chants. "Drop the Bomb," another notable gem from their lengthy discography, kept the energy level high and "Don't Touch That Stereo" was all raw, unencumbered funk. Обозначение обособленной велосипедной дорожки: highway=cycleway - основной тег линии, который указывает, что путь предназначен для движения на велосипедах. foot=no - явно запрещает движение пешеходов (если пешеходам запрещено находиться на этой дорожке). Если пешеходы разрешены, но дорожка разделена на зоны, используют foot=yes и segregated=yes/no . Велосипедная дорожка + тротуар: Комбинация тэгов для обозначения пешеходного тротуара, совмещённого с выделенной велосипедной дорожкой, которая конструктивно или визуально отделена от пешеходной зоны: highway=footway - обозначает, что данный объект является обустроенной дорожкой, предназначенной в первую очередь для пешеходов. footway=sidewalk - уточняет тип пешеходной дорожки. Этот тег указывает, что дорожка является тротуаром, то есть идет параллельно автомобильной дороге (обычно повторяя её геометрию). bicycle=designated - указывает на официальный юридический статус для велосипедистов. Это значит, что дорожка специально выделена/предназначена для движения на велосипеде (например, установлен соответствующий знак или нанесена разметка), а не просто «разрешена для транзита». segregated=yes - означает, что потоки пешеходов и велосипедистов разделены. Twenty-Five Years After 9/11 — Lessons from the World Trade Center Health Program Release For immediate release: September 10, 2026 CDC Media Relations (404) 639-3286 media@cdc.gov https://www.cdc.gov/media/ Paper examines 9/11-related health outcomes and lessons learned in the quarter century since the disaster. pages.text: Two Centuries After This Bronze Leg Emerged From a Scottish Bog, Archaeologists Believe It May Have Belonged to a Towering Statue of a Roman Emperor on Horseback Skip to main content Curator Fraser Hunter examines the bronze leg. Duncan McGlynn In 1820, a larger-than-life gilded bronze lower leg was pulled out of a bog in the Scottish Borders region. For more than two centuries, historians discredited the idea that the Roman-era artifact came from Scotland, instead assuming that it was hacked off a monument in England and hauled north by marauding tribes. But ahead of “ Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire ,” an exhibition at the National Museum of Scotland (NMS), researchers have determined that the so-called “Milsington leg” was not stolen from the south, nor was it violently severed. Instead, they posit that it formed part of a colossal equestrian statue of the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius that once stood in southern Scotland in the second century C.E., before it was dismantled by retreating Roman troops. “This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome’s second attempt at conquering Scotland,” Fraser Hunter , principal curator of prehistoric and Roman archaeology at NMS, says in a statement . The bronze leg shows no signs of being violently hacked off the larger statue. U.S. Gridded Methane Emissions The gridded EPA U.S. methane greenhouse gas inventory (gridded methane GHGI) includes time series of annual methane emission maps with 0.1° x 0.1° (~ 10 x 10 km) spatial and monthly temporal resolution for the contiguous United States (CONUS). This gridded methane inventory is designed to be consistent with methane emissions from the U.S. EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks (U.S. GHGI). The gridded methane GHGI dataset includes annual methane emission fluxes for over 25 inventory emission source categories, including those from agriculture, petroleum and natural gas systems, coal mining, and waste. Gridded methane emissions data are generated by allocating national annual U.S. GHGI methane emissions from individual source categories to a 0.1° x 0.1° CONUS grid, using a series of spatial and temporal 'proxy' datasets at the state, county, and grid levels. Where possible, proxy data are the same data used to develop the U.S. GHGI so that the gridded emissions can be, as closely as possible, a spatial and temporal representation of the national-level U.S. GHGI. Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures show. The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war. Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers. Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending. The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year. pages.text: Ukraine appeal IOC decision to reinstate Russia - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 By Elizabeth Botcherby BBC Sport journalist Published 29 July 2026 Ukraine's National Olympic Committee has launched an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport against the International Olympic Committee's decision to provisionally reinstate Russia to its competitions. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) suspended the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) in 2023 in response to the war in Ukraine but lifted the ban on 7 July 2026, stating it was "no longer applicable" , external . That decision opens the door for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games and is the latest step in the country's reinstatement to international competition, with the IOC previously recommending in December 2025 that federations readmit Russian and Belarusian Under-23 athletes. However, the National Olympic Committee (NOC) of Ukraine said the IOC's decision is "premature" and "violates" the Olympic Charter. "The position of the NOC of Ukraine is based on the fact that the IOC's decision was made prematurely and without proper verification of whether the violations - which led to the suspension of the ROC following the appeal by the NOC of Ukraine on October 6, 2023 - had actually been resolved," an NOC statement said. Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of Isfahan a day before Israel began attacking its nuclear sites last June. The US joined the strikes later that month. In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material. Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile. Under a 2015 nuclear deal, Iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3.67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both. Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade.
